description: ThinkHazard! is a web tool from the Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery (GFDRR) at the World Bank that classifies eleven natural hazards (river, urban and coastal flood, earthquake, landslide, tsunami, volcano, cyclone, water scarcity, extreme heat and wildfire) into high, medium, low or very low hazard levels for every country, province and district worldwide, with recommendations for reducing risk in project design. Levels are derived from the best available probabilistic or susceptibility datasets by testing intensity thresholds at three return periods and taking the maximum over each administrative unit (FAO GAUL levels 0 to 2). It is meant for screening and awareness, not for site-level design, and does not include real-time or historical event data. The underlying hazard datasets are listed per region and, when openly licensed, can be downloaded from the GFDRR Innovation Lab GeoNode; the tool's code is open source on GitHub and the site is free to use. Caveats are the coarse administrative aggregation, heterogeneous source resolutions and generic, sector-neutral recommendations. It supports hazard exposure screening of infrastructure portfolios, climate adaptation and resilience planning at an early stage, and points to more detailed layers such as Aqueduct Floods and the GEM seismic hazard map.
